blocks.text: The module documentation defines the chain shapes and the deliberate differences between SDK-shaped providers and Cloudflare REST. Imports, quota data, endpoint constants, and reasoning settings establish the policy used by later dispatch helpers.
blocks.title: Provider contract and quota tables

blocks.text: Custom exceptions distinguish retryable Cloudflare failures, unwinnable ledger steps, exhausted chains, and empty reasoning budgets. The retry-after helpers turn status codes, headers, and provider messages into bounded cooldown durations.
blocks.title: Error taxonomy and retry timing

blocks.text: Oversized prompts are reduced using provider limits, optional context markers, and whole JSON-list elements. The following helpers cache provider clients, obtain Cloudflare credentials, and isolate tracing failures from the real model call.
blocks.title: Prompt recovery and clients

blocks.anchor: def _call_step(client, model: str, system_prompt: str, user_content: str,
blocks.text: _call_step builds OpenAI-compatible chat requests and protects against reasoning-only empty responses. Tool-intent classification is a separate Groq-only logging path, while _call_cloudflare_step performs the REST equivalent and normalizes nested responses.
blocks.title: Provider call paths

blocks.text: Ledger behavior is counted globally and per session. Usage logging updates dated Redis records and emits events, while the cost and usage-ledger helpers write durable accounting data and probe streamed usage shapes.
blocks.title: Usage and cost records

blocks.anchor: def _max_tokens_for(provider: str, model: str, step: dict) -> int:
blocks.text: Token budgets combine explicit step overrides, model-family defaults, and verified provider limits. Header parsing supplies rate headroom, and cooperative shutdown and pause exceptions make waits interruptible.
blocks.title: Budgets, headers, and cancellation

blocks.anchor: def _remaining_chain_headroom(chain: list, from_index: int, estimated_tokens: int):
blocks.text: The ledger helpers look ahead for viable fallback steps, decide reroute versus wait, reserve estimates, reconcile actual usage, and handle finish reasons. Error buckets determine whether a step is shrunk, cooled, rerouted, or raised.
blocks.title: Ledger gate and error dispatch

blocks.anchor: def _run_chain_step(chain: list, index: int, is_last: bool, provider: str, model: str, key,
blocks.text: _run_chain_step owns the per-step retry loop and joins gating, tracing, provider invocation, accounting, continuation handling, and error dispatch. _walk_chain_once applies that loop to Cloudflare and SDK-shaped steps and returns either a result or exhaustion state.
blocks.title: One chain pass

blocks.anchor: def generate_text(system_prompt: str, user_content: str, chain: list, agent_name: str = "Agent",
blocks.text: generate_text executes one chain pass, returns complete or salvaged partial output, optionally rechecks a wholly rate-limited chain once, and raises ChainExhaustedError when no output can be produced.
blocks.title: Synchronous generation

blocks.anchor: async def _walk_chain_once_stream(system_prompt: str, user_content: str, chain: list,
blocks.text: The async path runs synchronous SDK iteration in a worker thread and forwards deltas through an asyncio queue. It preserves pre-first-chunk fallback, records usage at stream completion, and reports exhaustion through stream_completion.
blocks.title: Streaming generation

gotchas: Cloudflare usage is often absent even when its call succeeds
streaming skips Cloudflare and does not continue a truncated response
malformed requests are raised rather than hidden by fallback
credential values are read by name and are not part of this note
how_it_works: Builds cached OpenAI-shaped clients or sends the Cloudflare REST request
Checks cooldown and rate-ledger state before dispatching each chain step
Handles truncation, transient errors, authentication failures, and provider fallback
Provides synchronous generation and asynchronous chunk streaming paths
Writes usage counters, durable call logs, usage-ledger rows, and trace observations
inputs: provider credentials referenced by environment variable names
session, tier, path, domain, and agent metadata
outputs: usage, cost, cooldown, and ledger records
purpose: This module is the application boundary for chat-completion calls across several providers. It resolves provider clients, chooses bounded token budgets, classifies failures, and either falls back, retries with a safer prompt, or surfaces the failure. It also records usage, cost, ledger, and tracing data without allowing accounting failures to replace the model result.
side_effects: LLM provider network calls over SDKs or HTTPS
Redis reads and writes for cooldowns, usage, and ledger counters
Postgres writes for durable LLM call logs
worker-thread execution for synchronous provider streaming
summary: Runs provider-neutral LLM fallback chains with quota gating, retries, tracing, usage logging, and streaming.
